reasons.A: Closest movement: medium sentences punctuated by blunt short verdicts ('It was nothing of the sort', 'We are only now getting round to them') that echo the author's dry, homely wit and plain period diction.
reasons.B: Right period register and earnest-ironic stance ('rather slow learners'), but sentences run longer and more uniformly balanced, missing the author's abrupt short turns.
reasons.C: Modern diction and framing ('with a sneer', 'deserves a real answer', 'lying about having graduated') and an explanatory, contemporary-essay tone that departs from the author's period voice.
